title: How the pieces move
intro: One lesson per piece: where it can go, how it captures, and a little challenge to try it out.

lessons.title: The rook
lessons.summary: Straight lines, as far as it likes.

steps.text: The rook moves in straight lines: up, down, left or right, as many squares as it likes.
Move the rook to the ringed square.
steps.hint: Slide the rook along its row to the right.
steps.ifWrong: The ringed square is at the end of the rook's row.
steps.ifRight: Good: the rook slid all the way along the rank.

steps.text: Pieces capture by moving onto an enemy piece's square. The captured piece leaves the board. Pieces cannot jump over others: your own pawn on d6 blocks the rook's way up.
Capture the black knight with your rook.
steps.hint: The knight is on the same row as your rook.
steps.ifWrong: That does not capture the knight. It is on the rook's row.

steps.text: Your rook can take a knight or a bishop. Take the piece nobody protects.
steps.hint: Look at the pawn on b7. What does it guard?
steps.ifWrong: Look for a capture where you do not lose the rook back.
steps.ifRight: Right: the knight was unprotected, so it is a free piece.

feedback.a1a6: The pawn on b7 protects that bishop. After bxa6 you lose your rook (5) for a bishop (3).

steps.text: The bishop moves diagonally, as far as it likes. It always stays on squares of the same colour.
Capture the black rook with your bishop.
steps.hint: Follow the diagonal up and to the left.
steps.ifWrong: Bishops move only diagonally. Which diagonal leads to the rook?

steps.text: Bishops only move diagonally. Which black piece can your bishop capture? Take it.
steps.hint: The rook is not on a diagonal from your bishop.
steps.ifWrong: That does not capture anything. Follow the diagonals from the bishop.
steps.ifRight: Yes, the knight was on the bishop's diagonal.

steps.text: Give check with the bishop.
steps.hint: Which diagonal leads to the black king?
steps.ifWrong: The king is not attacked. Find a diagonal that points at e8.

steps.text: The queen moves like a rook and a bishop together: straight or diagonal, as far as it likes. That makes her the strongest piece.
Capture the knight with your queen.
steps.hint: The knight is on a diagonal.
steps.ifWrong: Follow the queen's diagonals to find the knight.

steps.text: Capture a rook without losing your queen.
steps.hint: One of the rooks is protected by a pawn.
steps.ifWrong: Look for a rook your queen can take safely.
steps.ifRight: Well done: that rook had no protection.

feedback.d2b4: The pawn on c5 protects that rook. After cxb4 your queen (9) is gone for a rook (5).
feedback.d2e3: Clever: a check that also attacks the rook! It wins the rook next move. Here, just take the free rook now.

lessons.title: The king
lessons.summary: One step at a time, never into danger.

steps.text: The king moves one square in any direction.
The king may never move into check: it cannot step onto a square an enemy piece attacks. Here the black rook guards the whole e-file.
Capture the pawn with your king.
steps.hint: The pawn is right next to your king.
steps.ifWrong: The pawn is one step away. Take it!
steps.ifRight: The king can capture too, one step at a time.

steps.text: Your king can capture one of the pawns. The other is protected, so the king may not take it. Capture the free pawn.
steps.hint: The pawn on f5 guards one of them.
steps.ifWrong: Capture one of the pawns next to your king.
steps.ifRight: Right. The pawn on e4 was protected by f5, so taking it would walk into check.

steps.text: The knight moves in an L: two squares in one direction, then one square to the side. From the middle it can reach eight squares.
The knight is the only piece that can jump over others. From the start it hops straight over its pawns.
Capture the bishop with your knight.
steps.hint: Two squares up, one to the right.
steps.ifWrong: Remember the L: two squares one way, then one to the side.

steps.text: Your knight can reach the black queen in one jump. Take it.
steps.hint: Two squares up and one to the right.
steps.ifWrong: Count the L: two squares one way, one to the side.

steps.text: A knight can attack two pieces at once. Jump to a square that attacks both the king and the rook.
steps.hint: Look for a square an L-jump away from both e8 and a8.
steps.ifWrong: That attacks only one of them (or none). Find the square that hits both.
steps.ifRight: A fork! The king must move, and then you take the rook.

lessons.title: The pawn
lessons.summary: Forward to move, diagonal to capture.

steps.text: Pawns move straight forward, one square at a time. On its very first move, a pawn may go two squares.
Pawns capture differently: one square diagonally forward. A pawn can never capture straight ahead, and never moves backwards.
Capture with your pawn. Take the more valuable piece.
steps.ifRight: Yes: a pawn for a knight is a great deal.

feedback.e4d5: That wins a pawn (1). The knight (3) is worth more.

steps.text: Move your pawn two squares forward.
steps.hint: From its starting square, a pawn may jump two squares.
steps.ifWrong: Move the pawn, two squares straight ahead.
